analyst_view.overall: Castellón are 2nd with 30 points, nine wins from 13 and by far the league's best defence (5 conceded), and won 1-0 at Valladolid last weekend; Pablo Hernández's side keep a lot of the ball (7,285 passes, most in this pairing) and Brignani's long injury is already in the numbers. Eldense are 15th with 17 points after beating ten-man Sabadell 2-0 under Javi Calleja; Juan Larios is back from suspension and Guille Macho was still injured last weekend. Eldense are the more booked side (37 yellows to Castellón's 25), which the numbers already weigh through momentum. News was thin: I found no fresh preview with team news for this match and no referee yet, so the view rests on form and season stats.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 2.0 of them Castellón's. Castellón have scored 24 and conceded only 5 in 13, and Eldense have conceded 19, all of which is already in the ratings; with no new absences found on either side, I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, 5.7 of them Castellón's, a possession side at home against a team that tends to defend deep away. Nothing new points either way, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, with Eldense expected to pick up 3.5 of them: they have 37 yellows and foul more than Castellón, which the numbers already count. No referee is named yet and nothing suggests extra tension, so I stay at 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.5 shots. Castellón dominate the ball at home and Eldense have 134 shots in 14 games, close to Castellón's 132 in 13; with no lineup news to change that picture, I stay at 24.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Castellón's defence allows very little and both sides are near full strength apart from known absences, so I stay at 8.7.
